Title: Valid admin login grants workspace access
Preconditions: Use the published quick-sign-in credential admin / admin123.
Steps:
1. Open the Orbit sign-in page - https://orbit-platform.wasmer.app/
2. Enter username `admin`.
3. Enter password `admin123`.
4. Select Sign In to Workspace.
Expected Result: The user is authenticated and the Orbit workspace is displayed with ADMIN privileges and project/board controls.

Title: Valid member login grants member-level workspace access
Preconditions: Use the published quick-sign-in credential alex / alex123.
Steps:
1. Open the sign-in page.
2. Enter `alex` and `alex123`.
3. Sign in.
Expected Result: The workspace opens as the member account and member-appropriate controls are shown.

Title: Valid viewer login grants viewer-level workspace access
Preconditions: Use the published quick-sign-in credential sam / sam123.
Steps:
1. Open the sign-in page.
2. Enter `sam` and `sam123`.
3. Sign in.
Expected Result: The workspace opens as the viewer account and viewer restrictions are enforced.

Title: Invalid password is rejected
Preconditions: A valid username exists.
Steps:
1. Enter a valid username.
2. Enter an incorrect password.
3. Sign in.
Expected Result: Authentication fails, the user remains on the sign-in screen, and an invalid-credentials message is shown.

Title: Unknown username is rejected
Preconditions: None.
Steps:
1. Enter an unknown username.
2. Enter any password.
3. Sign in.
Expected Result: Authentication fails without entering the workspace and an invalid-credentials message is shown.

Title: Required login fields are validated
Preconditions: None.
Steps:
1. Leave username and password blank.
2. Attempt to sign in.
3. Repeat with one field blank.
Expected Result: The form prevents submission and clearly indicates the missing required value(s).

Title: Logout invalidates the active session
Preconditions: A user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Sign in.
2. Select Logout.
3. Attempt to access the workspace using the browser Back button or a previously loaded workspace URL.
Expected Result: The session is invalidated; protected project/Kanban data is not accessible and the sign-in screen is shown.

Title: Post-logout session data is purged
Preconditions: A user is signed in and has loaded workspace data.
Steps:
1. Sign in and load the workspace.
2. Log out.
3. Observe the logout confirmation/state.
Expected Result: The logout flow reports session invalidation, cookie deletion, and clearing of project/Kanban data.

Title: Create project with required fields
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Create Project.
2. Enter a unique project key.
3. Enter a project name.
4. Optionally enter a description.
5. Select Create Project.
Expected Result: The project is created and becomes selectable in the project control.

Title: Project creation blocks missing project key
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Create Project.
2. Enter a project name only.
3. Select Create Project.
Expected Result: The project is not created and the required Project Key field is flagged.

Title: Project creation blocks missing project name
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Create Project.
2. Enter a project key only.
3. Select Create Project.
Expected Result: The project is not created and the required Project Name field is flagged.

Title: Default Kanban workflow is provisioned for a new project
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Create a valid new project.
2. Open the project's board/workflow configuration.
Expected Result: The new project has the documented five default Kanban columns.

Title: Add a custom Kanban column
Preconditions: A project exists and admin can configure its workflow.
Steps:
1. Open Configure Kanban Columns.
2. Enter a unique stage name.
3. Select Add Stage.
4. Save the configuration.
Expected Result: The custom stage is added and appears in the configured workflow order.

Title: Configure Kanban column order and titles
Preconditions: A project exists.
Steps:
1. Open column configuration.
2. Add or modify workflow stages.
3. Save the configuration.
4. Reopen the configuration.
Expected Result: The saved stage names and ordering persist after reopening.

Title: Cancel project creation does not create a project
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Create Project.
2. Enter otherwise valid project data.
3. Select Cancel.
4. Open the project selector.
Expected Result: No new project is present.

Title: Project selector switches the active project
Preconditions: At least two projects are available.
Steps:
1. Select Project A.
2. Note displayed board data.
3. Select Project B.
Expected Result: The workspace context switches to Project B and its data is displayed.

Title: Create and schedule sprint with required name
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in and a project exists.
Steps:
1. Open Sprint Management.
2. Select Plan New Sprint.
3. Enter a sprint name.
4. Enter goal and valid start/end dates.
5. Select Create & Schedule Sprint.
Expected Result: The sprint is created/scheduled and appears in the sprint list.

Title: Sprint creation blocks missing sprint name
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Plan New Sprint.
2. Leave Sprint Name blank.
3. Enter other valid fields.
4. Select Create & Schedule Sprint.
Expected Result: The sprint is not created and Sprint Name is reported as required.

Title: Sprint date range is validated
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Create a sprint with an end date earlier than its start date.
2. Submit the sprint.
Expected Result: The invalid date range is rejected with clear validation feedback.

Title: Start sprint changes sprint state to active
Preconditions: A planned sprint exists.
Steps:
1. Open Sprint Management.
2. Select the planned sprint.
3. Start the sprint.
Expected Result: The sprint becomes the active/current sprint and its state is reflected in the UI.

Title: Complete sprint summarizes completed and incomplete issues
Preconditions: An active sprint contains at least one completed and one incomplete issue.
Steps:
1. Open Complete Sprint.
2. Review the completed and incomplete counts.
3. Complete the sprint.
Expected Result: Counts are accurate and the sprint is marked complete.

Title: Incomplete sprint issues can be carried over
Preconditions: An active sprint contains incomplete issues and a destination sprint exists.
Steps:
1. Complete the active sprint.
2. Select a destination sprint for incomplete issues.
3. Confirm completion.
Expected Result: Incomplete issues are moved to the selected destination sprint and remain available.

Title: Create issue with required title
Preconditions: A project exists and user can create issues.
Steps:
1. Open Create Issue.
2. Select project and optionally sprint.
3. Enter a title.
4. Set priority, status, type, points, assignee, and tags.
5. Create the issue.
Expected Result: The issue is created with a unique issue key and the supplied field values.

Title: Issue creation blocks missing title
Preconditions: A project exists.
Steps:
1. Open Create Issue.
2. Leave Title blank.
3. Select Create Issue.
Expected Result: The issue is not created and Title is flagged as required.

Title: Issue accepts Markdown description
Preconditions: A project exists.
Steps:
1. Create or edit an issue.
2. Enter Markdown formatting in Description.
3. Save changes.
4. Reopen the issue.
Expected Result: The description is saved and rendered/supported as Markdown without data loss.

Title: Issue supports priority, type, status, points, sprint, assignee, and tags
Preconditions: A project exists and team members are available.
Steps:
1. Create an issue.
2. Populate each supported field with valid values.
3. Save.
4. Reopen the issue.
Expected Result: All selected values persist and are displayed correctly.

Title: Acceptance checklist items can be added and completed
Preconditions: An issue exists.
Steps:
1. Open an issue.
2. Add an acceptance criterion.
3. Mark it complete.
4. Observe the completion counter.
Expected Result: The criterion is stored, its completion state changes, and the counter updates accurately.

Title: Issue comments can be posted
Preconditions: An issue exists.
Steps:
1. Open an issue.
2. Enter a comment.
3. Select Post Comment.
Expected Result: The comment appears in Discussion & Comments with the correct author/context.

Title: Issue supports image attachment
Preconditions: An issue exists and a valid image file is available.
Steps:
1. Open an issue.
2. Add an image attachment.
3. Save.
4. Reopen the issue.
Expected Result: The attachment is uploaded, associated with the issue, and can be previewed.

Title: Issue attachment can be previewed and downloaded
Preconditions: An issue has an image attachment.
Steps:
1. Open the attachment preview.
2. Select Download.
Expected Result: The attachment preview displays the correct file and download action retrieves the file.

Title: Issue changes persist after Save Changes
Preconditions: An existing issue is available.
Steps:
1. Edit title, description, priority, points, sprint, or tags.
2. Select Save Changes.
3. Close and reopen the issue.
Expected Result: Saved values persist exactly and are displayed after reopening.

Title: Keyword filter returns matching issues
Preconditions: Multiple issues exist with distinct titles/keys/tags.
Steps:
1. Enter a distinctive keyword in the issue filter.
2. Observe results.
Expected Result: Only matching issues are displayed.

Title: Issue key search returns the exact issue
Preconditions: At least one issue exists.
Steps:
1. Enter a known issue key in the filter.
2. Observe results.
Expected Result: The matching issue is returned and unrelated issues are excluded.

Title: Combined filters narrow results
Preconditions: Issues exist with different types, tags, priorities, assignees, and columns.
Steps:
1. Apply two or more filters.
2. Observe results.
3. Clear one filter.
Expected Result: Results satisfy all active filters and expand appropriately when a filter is cleared.

Title: Clear filters restores the full issue set
Preconditions: Multiple issues exist.
Steps:
1. Apply keyword and/or dropdown filters.
2. Select Clear.
Expected Result: All filters reset and the unfiltered issue list is restored.

Title: Admin can create a team member
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open User Management.
2. Select Add New User.
3. Enter unique username, password, full name, email, and role.
4. Select Create & Add User.
Expected Result: The user is created and appears in the Team Directory with the assigned role.

Title: User creation validates required fields
Preconditions: Admin user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Add New User.
2. Leave one or more required fields blank.
3. Submit.
Expected Result: The user is not created and each missing required field is identified.

Title: User role controls permitted actions
Preconditions: Admin, member, and viewer accounts are available.
Steps:
1. Sign in as admin, member, and viewer in separate sessions.
2. Compare project, sprint, issue, and user-management controls.
3. Attempt restricted operations.
Expected Result: Each role can perform only its authorized actions; restricted operations are hidden or rejected.

Title: Admin can change another user's name
Preconditions: Admin is signed in and another user exists.
Steps:
1. Open the user's edit-name action.
2. Enter a new full name.
3. Save.
Expected Result: The user's full name is updated everywhere it is displayed.

Title: Password change enforces minimum length
Preconditions: A user account exists and password management is available.
Steps:
1. Open Change User Password.
2. Enter a password shorter than four characters.
3. Submit.
Expected Result: The password is rejected with validation feedback and the existing password remains valid.

Title: User can update own profile name
Preconditions: A user is signed in.
Steps:
1. Open Edit Profile.
2. Enter a new full name.
3. Select Save Profile Name.
Expected Result: The profile name is updated and reflected in the workspace.

Title: Notification unread count is displayed
Preconditions: The account has at least one unread notification.
Steps:
1. Open the workspace.
2. Observe Notifications count.
3. Open notifications.
Expected Result: The unread count matches the number of unread notifications.

Title: Mark all notifications as read clears unread state
Preconditions: At least one unread notification exists.
Steps:
1. Open Notifications.
2. Select Mark all as read.
Expected Result: All notifications become read and the unread count becomes zero.

Title: Notification filter switches between all and unread
Preconditions: Both read and unread notifications exist.
Steps:
1. Open Notifications.
2. Select Unread.
3. Select All.
Expected Result: Unread shows only unread items; All restores both read and unread items.

Title: c shortcut opens Create New Issue
Preconditions: User is signed in and not typing into a field.
Steps:
1. Press `c`.
2. Observe the UI.
Expected Result: The Create New Issue modal opens.

Title: slash shortcut focuses issue filter
Preconditions: User is signed in and not typing into another input.
Steps:
1. Press `/`.
2. Observe focus.
Expected Result: The issue filter/search input receives keyboard focus.

Title: Esc closes open modal or preview
Preconditions: A modal or attachment preview is open.
Steps:
1. Press `Esc`.
2. Observe the UI.
Expected Result: The currently open modal or preview closes without unintended data changes.

Title: Question-mark shortcut opens keyboard guide
Preconditions: User is signed in and not typing into a field.
Steps:
1. Press `?`.
2. Observe the UI.
Expected Result: The Keyboard Shortcuts guide opens and lists the supported shortcuts.
